task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal on floor)
separability from player counts and talent
methodological_questions: Does lineup coverage vary enough within team-seasons to be tested?
Is coverage separable from talent and role counts (collinearity, residual variation)?
Does the talent control behave (sign, stability, placebo)?
How are organizer, shaper and terminal labels derived, and are they outcome-derived?
Is there exposure sparsity in lineup-possession cells?

historical_evidence.finding: Structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability: C1a rho=+0.079 p=0.0882 CI[-0.114,+0.234]; C1b rho=+0.095 p=0.0738; robustness thresholds also fail. Recorded as B_powered_null, n=117 across 30 franchises, limited by small sample and low power / large MDE.

Structural influence is not reducible to usage: F1a cosine R2=0.094 (residual share 0.906) and F1b split-half residual rho about +0.67 to +0.69 were both CONFIRMED in two records ([prior work], [prior work]). Limited by low measurement reliability.

Absence validation: real absences moved structure (V1 confirmed, 16/23 above p95), but the simulation's magnitude prediction (V2a rho=+0.288 p=0.077; V2b p=0.115) failed with a wide CI. Limited by small sample.

Adaptation quality vs talent for series wins: after talent control the adaptation coefficient had p=0.275. Recorded as A_unanswerable: n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality. Limited by confounding and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Team-level (franchise) rank correlation between structural concentration and defensive vulnerability
failed_approaches.why: Powered null: the CI spans 0 with only 30 franchises, so the effect is not detected. Recorded limitations are low power / large MDE and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of structural change under absence with a leave-one-out simulation
failed_approaches.why: Small sample (n=23 cases), wide CI, recorded as untestable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Separating an adaptation effect from talent at the series level
failed_approaches.why: Confounding with roster quality and a small sample (about 55 series); recorded as A_unanswerable.

evidence_establishes: Per FAM:[prior work], structural influence measures are largely not reducible to usage (residual share about 0.90) and the usage residual is reproducible at the player level (split-half rho about +0.67), so a structural component separable from counts has been supported at the player level.
Per [prior work][prior work], FAM:[prior work] and [prior work][prior work], team-level or series-level analyses with about 23 to 117 units had insufficient power or were confounded by talent.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record measured lineup-level coverage (at least one organizer, shaper and terminal) or its within-team variation.
No retrieved record tested whether a coverage indicator is separable from role counts and talent at the lineup or possession level.
No retrieved record examined how a talent control behaves (sign, stability, placebo) for a coverage variable.
None of the retrieved records establish how organizer, shaper and terminal labels are assigned or whether they are outcome-derived.
own_inferences: The question is a measurement-validity and diagnostic question (variation, separability, behaviour of a control), not an outcome-effect hypothesis. The 90 team-seasons are not the binding unit, because coverage can be computed at lineup-stint or possession level (420,993 possessions), which makes it testable much more easily than the team-level tests that failed.

Coverage is mechanically related to the count of role-holders on the floor: a lineup with zero organizers has zero coverage by construction. Separability must therefore be tested against the count of role-holders and against a null built from random role assignment with counts fixed (permutation), not simply by a correlation.

FAM:[prior work]'s player-level residual reliability supports using usage-residual labels, but reliability of the role labels near thresholds is likely the weak point and could generate spurious within-team variation.
The talent control 'behaves' only if pre-specified criteria are set, for example expected sign, no sign flip across specifications, and a null placebo using shuffled talent.
uncertainties: How the organizer, shaper and terminal roles are defined, and with what thresholds, is not stated in the task or in the retrieved records.
Whether roles are assigned from the same possessions used to compute coverage (an outcome-derived label) is unknown.
The talent metric (for example on/off, net rating, minutes-weighted) is unspecified, and a talent metric computed on the same possessions would be circular.
The distribution of lineup minutes (the effective number of distinct lineups per team-season) has not been seen.
I did not call follow-up tools, so FAM records were not read in full and [source] [source] were not inspected.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved failures ([prior work][prior work], FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work]) all involved small-n team- or series-level inference and talent confounding. That pushed the design to a lineup/possession-level, descriptive and diagnostic test with permutation nulls and clustering by team-season, instead of a team-level correlational test. FAM:[prior work] supports the idea that a structural component separable from usage exists at the player level, which raised confidence that separability is plausible.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels near thresholds may be unreliable (FAM:[prior work] records low measurement reliability as a limitation), so coverage variation could reflect label noise.
Many lineups have few possessions, so lineup-level coverage cells may be sparse unless aggregated by stint or by lineup-minute.

prior_work.summary: Player-level separability of structural influence from usage was supported (FAM:[prior work]). The lineup coverage construct, its within-team variation and its talent-control behaviour have not been addressed by any retrieved record. Team-level outcome tests ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) and absence prediction (FAM:[prior work]) were null or untestable because of small n and confounding.

risks.text: Coverage is a function of how many role-holders are on the floor, so separability from counts can be mechanically bounded; a fixed-count permutation null is needed.
If role labels or the talent measure use the same possessions or outcomes as the coverage test, separability and talent-control results are circular.
Threshold-based role labels may flip across seasons or split halves, inflating apparent within-team variation.
Lineup coverage is correlated with talent, minutes, starters and garbage time; the talent control may over- or under-adjust.
Sparse lineup possession counts make coverage and talent estimates noisy, shrinking apparent variation or inflating it.
Role definitions and pace/style shift across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons, and the 2025-26 playoffs data are partial before 2026-06-21.
If analysis is aggregated to the 90 team-seasons, power is as poor as in [prior work][prior work]; team-level analyses should not be the confirmatory unit.
Three sub-claims (variation, separability, talent control) across several specifications and seasons require a fixed family.

design.estimand: Three pre-specified estimands: (1) within-team share of variance in lineup coverage (indicator and count-weighted) via variance decomposition into between team-season and within team-season components; (2) incremental separability: the share of coverage variance not explained by the number of role-holders on the floor and lineup talent, compared with the same quantity under a fixed-count permutation null; (3) talent-control behaviour: the coefficient of lineup talent on coverage, with sign, stability across seasons and placebo behaviour.
design.unit: Lineup stint (a continuous interval with one five-man unit), weighted by possessions; sensitivity at the possession level. Inference clustered by team-season (90 clusters). Team-season aggregation is descriptive only.
design.sample: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons plus playoffs as a development/confirmation split by season (tune thresholds on 2022-23 and 2023-24, confirm on 2024-25). 2025-26 regular season (complete) used as a holdout; the 2025-26 playoffs are excluded or labelled partial/complete by data version. Exclude lineups with fewer than a pre-set number of possessions (for example 20) and garbage-time stints, with both exclusion thresholds fixed before analysis and a sensitivity analysis without them.
design.power: Unit is the stint/possession (420,993 possessions) but the effective sample size is bounded by 90 team-season clusters. Report cluster-bootstrap CIs and minimum detectable effect for the within-team variance share and for the talent coefficient. Pre-specify that variance-share claims require a CI excluding 0.10 (or another stated threshold), and that no claim is made when the CI is wider than a pre-set width.
design.controls: Role labels derived from out-of-sample data (prior season or the odd-numbered games) than the coverage test (even games). Talent measured from a separate data split and not from the possessions being tested, for example a player-level rating from prior season or odd games, with shrinkage; also run a minutes-based talent proxy. Control for the number of role-holders, starters on floor, game period and score margin (garbage time), and team-season fixed effects.
design.falsification: (a) Fixed-count permutation: shuffle the role assignment across players within team-season holding counts fixed; observed separability must exceed the null. (b) Shuffled-talent placebo: replacing talent with a permuted lineup talent should give a null coefficient. (c) Split-half stability of role labels (FAM:[prior work]-style) must pass a pre-set reliability bar. (d) Label-noise stress test: perturb thresholds and show that conclusions persist. The claim fails if variation or separability disappears under any of (a)-(d).
design.multiplicity: Three confirmatory claims (variation, separability, talent-control behaviour) with Holm correction at family alpha=0.05; threshold and season sensitivity analyses are labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if: within-team variance share has a lower CI bound above the pre-set threshold; the permutation-null-adjusted separability is above null with the CI excluding 0; the talent coefficient has the pre-specified sign, is stable across seasons, and the placebo is null; and role-label reliability passes. Rejected if the CIs are narrow and exclude the thresholds. Untestable if label reliability fails or fewer than a pre-set share of team-seasons have multiple lineups with adequate exposure. Any failure of the permutation or placebo checks is reported as an artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and the derived play-type possession graph database as of 2026-07-13: 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete; 2025-26 regular season complete (from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs complete (from 2026-06-21). Freeze file hashes and graph-database snapshot before analysis.
